title: weather.client.WeatherClient
---



```python
weather.client.WeatherClient(latitude, longitude)
```

Client for fetching weather data from Open-Meteo API.
Handles the low-level API interactions, parameter building, and response parsing.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type             | Description                | Default    |
|-----------|------------------|----------------------------|------------|
| latitude  | [float](`float`) | Latitude of the location.  | _required_ |
| longitude | [float](`float`) | Longitude of the location. | _required_ |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#e6825db2 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Fetching from Open-Meteo requires a live network connection.
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.weather import WeatherClient
client = WeatherClient(latitude=52.52, longitude=13.405)
df = client.fetch_archive(
    start=pd.Timestamp("2023-01-01", tz="UTC"),
    end=pd.Timestamp("2023-01-02", tz="UTC"),
)
print(df.head())
```
:::


Construction and attribute inspection do not require a network call:

::: {#12d34de6 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from spotforecast2_safe.weather.client import WeatherClient

client = WeatherClient(latitude=52.52, longitude=13.405)
assert client.latitude == 52.52
assert client.longitude == 13.405
print(f"WeatherClient at ({client.latitude}, {client.longitude})")
print("HOURLY_PARAMS count:", len(client.HOURLY_PARAMS))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
WeatherClient at (52.52, 13.405)
HOURLY_PARAMS count: 15
```
:::
:::


## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [fetch_archive](#spotforecast2_safe.weather.client.WeatherClient.fetch_archive) | Fetch historical data from Archive API. |
| [fetch_forecast](#spotforecast2_safe.weather.client.WeatherClient.fetch_forecast) | Fetch forecast data from Forecast API. |

### fetch_archive { #spotforecast2_safe.weather.client.WeatherClient.fetch_archive }

```python
weather.client.WeatherClient.fetch_archive(start, end, timezone='UTC')
```

Fetch historical data from Archive API.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                           | Description                            | Default    |
|----------|------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|------------|
| start    | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Start date for the historical data.    | _required_ |
| end      | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | End date for the historical data.      | _required_ |
| timezone | [str](`str`)                                   | Timezone for the data (default "UTC"). | `'UTC'`    |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

::: {#b4368b7d .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Requires a live connection to archive-api.open-meteo.com.
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.weather import WeatherClient
client = WeatherClient(latitude=52.52, longitude=13.405)
df = client.fetch_archive(
    start=pd.Timestamp("2023-01-01", tz="UTC"),
    end=pd.Timestamp("2023-01-02", tz="UTC"),
)
print(df.head())
```
:::


### fetch_forecast { #spotforecast2_safe.weather.client.WeatherClient.fetch_forecast }

```python
weather.client.WeatherClient.fetch_forecast(
    days_ahead,
    timezone='UTC',
    past_days=0,
)
```

Fetch forecast data from Forecast API.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Default    |
|------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| days_ahead | [int](`int`) | Number of days ahead for the forecast.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | _required_ |
| timezone   | [str](`str`) | Timezone for the data (default "UTC").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `'UTC'`    |
| past_days  | [int](`int`) | Recent past days to also request from the forecast endpoint via Open-Meteo's `past_days` parameter (0--92). The archive endpoint lags several days, so `past_days` lets the forecast endpoint backfill that recent window; without it the `[now - archive_lag, today]` range is fetched by neither endpoint and is later carried forward as a flat line. | `0`        |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

::: {#1ccb7058 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Requires a live connection to api.open-meteo.com.
from spotforecast2_safe.weather import WeatherClient
client = WeatherClient(latitude=52.52, longitude=13.405)
df = client.fetch_forecast(days_ahead=7)
print(df.head())
```
:::
